titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Journey to Gaza and the Mistaken King (ch. 33–34)
part: ch. 33–34 — The Journey to Gaza and the Mistaken King
about: The Queen sends her son to Solomon in the care of her merchant Tamrin, with provisions and a message: the throne of Ethiopia is to pass henceforth to a male of Solomon's line, idolatry is forbidden, and she asks for a relic of Zion. At Gaza, a city said to be Ethiopian, which the chronicle links to Acts 8, the people take the boy for Solomon himself and rush to honor him. Couriers sent to Jerusalem find the real king and describe the stranger, who is the image of Solomon and David. Solomon, troubled, recalls that God has foiled his plan to father many sons, as Paul says, and the chapter closes on the oath to David and the Ethiopian king as heir of Zion.

sentences.t: ፴ወ፫ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ ወረደ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ።
sentences.l: 33. How went-down king-of Ethiopia.
sentences.i: Chapter 33: How the King of Ethiopia Went Down
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፴ወ፫ is 33 (spoken ሠላሳ ወሠለስቱ, śälasa wä-śälästu); the ወ inside the numeral is 'and', as in ፳ወ፪ elsewhere. ዘከመ 'how' (ዘ- + ከመ, 'in the manner that') introduces the account; ወረደ 'he went down' (ወረደ 'descend'); the heading does not say where, and I take it as the boy's journey down toward Palestine (?). ንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ 'king of Ethiopia' is a title given to him in advance, since the chapter is about him (and, in the story's view, the future king). Construct chain: ንጉሠ 'king of' + ኢትዮጵያ 'Ethiopia'.

sentences.t: ወጸውዐቶ ፡ ለተምሪን ፡ ሊቀ ፡ ነጋድያኒሃ ፡ ወትበሎ ፡ ተደለው ፡ ለመንግድከ ፡ ወውስዶ ፡ ለዝንቱ ፡ ወልድ ፡ እስመ ፡ አጽሐበኒ ፡ ሌሊተ ፡ ወመዐልተ ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ በሕቁ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-summoned-him to-Tamrin chief-of her-merchants, and-she-said-to-him: Prepare for-your-journey and-take this son, for he-wearied-me night and-day exceedingly by-his-ሕቁ (?);
sentences.i: She summoned Tamrin, the chief of her merchants, and said to him: "Make ready for your journey and take this son, for he has worn me out, night and day, exceedingly, by his ሕቁ (?);
sentences.n: ወጸውዐቶ 'and she summoned him' (ጸውዐ 'call', 3rd feminine singular perfect, + -ቶ 'him'); ለተምሪን: ለ- marks the object here, as it often does with persons (the accusative sign, not 'to'). ሊቀ ነጋድያኒሃ 'chief of her merchants' (ሊቅ 'chief' in the construct, ነጋድያን plural of ነጋዲ 'merchant' + -ሃ 'her'). ወትበሎ is the spelling of ወትቤሎ 'and she said to him' (as ይበላ was read in ch. 31). ተደለው 'prepare!' (imperative of ተደለወ) with ለመንግድከ 'for your journey' (መንግድ 'road, journey'); ወውስዶ 'and take him!' (imperative of ወሰደ). እስመ አጽሐበኒ is uncertain: I take አጽሐበ as 'wore out, wearied' from context, with -ኒ 'me' (?). ሌሊተ ወመዐልተ 'by night and by day' (accusatives of time); ፈድፋደ 'exceedingly'. በሕቁ is unclear to me: I cannot place it and give no sense for it; the English leaves it in Geʿez (?). The speaker is the Queen; Tamrin is the caravan-leader of ch. 7 onward.

sentences.t: ወታበጽሖ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወታገብኦ ፡ በዳኅን ፡ ዝየ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ሠምረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ።
sentences.l: and-bring-him to king, and-restore-him in-safety here, if willed God God-of Israel.
sentences.i: and bring him to the king, and bring him back here safely, if God, the God of Israel, wills it."
sentences.n: ወታበጽሖ 'and bring him' (አበጽሐ, causative of በጽሐ 'arrive': 'cause to arrive', 2nd masculine imperfect used as a command, + -ኦ 'him', merged into the final ሖ); ወታገብኦ 'and bring him back' (አግብአ 'return' transitively). በዳኅን 'in safety' (ዳኅን 'safe'). ለእመ ሠምረ እግዚኣብሔር 'if God is pleased, wills' (ለእመ 'if'; ሠምረ 'be pleased, will'). The phrase repeats the boy's own words at the end of ch. 32 (በፈቃደ እግዚኣብሔር አምላከ እስራኤል).

sentences.t: ወተደለወት ፡ ሥንቀ ፡ በከመ ፡ ብዕሎሙ ፡ ወክብሮሙ ፡ ወኵሎ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ዘይትፈቀድ ፡ ለፍኖት ፡ ወዘይትወሀብ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ወዘይከውን ፡ ዕረፍተ ፡ ለፍኖት ፤
sentences.l: And-she-prepared provision according-to their-wealth and-their-honor, and-all goods which is-needed for-journey, and-which is-given gift to-king, and-which will-be rest(?) for-journey;
sentences.i: She prepared provisions suited to their wealth and rank, and all the goods needed for the road, those to be given as a gift to the king and those that would ease the journey;
sentences.n: ተደለወት 'she prepared' (ተደለወ, feminine perfect; the same verb as the imperative ተደለው above). ሥንቀ 'provisions' (accusative). በከመ ብዕሎሙ ወክብሮሙ 'according to their wealth and their honor': ብዕል 'wealth', ክብር 'honor, rank', + -ሙ 'their'. ዘይትፈቀድ 'which is needed' (ዘ- relative + ተፈቀደ 'be needed, be wanted', a passive-reflexive imperfect), ዘይትወሀብ 'which is given' (ተወሀበ 'be given'), ዘይከውን 'which will be' (ኮነ). አምኃ 'gift, tribute' (accusative; the word recurs in unit 20). ዕረፍተ ለፍኖት 'rest for the road' (ዕረፍት 'rest, relief'); I read 'something to ease the journey'. The three ዘ- clauses are in a list, each describing the goods.

sentences.t: ወአስተዳለወት ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትፈንዎ ፡ ወወሀበት ፡ ለመኳንንትኒ ፡ እለ ፡ የሐውሩ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ወወሀበቶሙ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ ዘይትፈቀድ ፡ ለፍኖት ።
sentences.l: And-she-made-ready everything that she-send-him, and-she-gave to-the-nobles-too who go with-him, and-she-gave-them much goods which is-needed for-journey.
sentences.i: She made everything ready to send him off, and she gave also to the nobles who were going with him, and gave them much of what was needed for the road.
sentences.n: ወአስተዳለወት 'and she made ready' (አስተዳለወ, a causative-reflexive of the same root as ተደለወ). ከመ ትፈንዎ 'that she might send him' (ፈነወ 'send', subjunctive 3rd feminine, + -ዎ 'him'). ወወሀበት ለመኳንንትኒ: መኳንንት 'nobles, officers' (plural of መኰንን); ለ- marks the recipient; the enclitic -ኒ is 'also, indeed'. እለ የሐውሩ 'who go' (እለ is the plural relative 'those who', የሐውሩ imperfect of ሖረ); ምስሌሁ 'with him'. ወሀበቶሙ 'she gave them' (ወሀበ + -ቶሙ). ብዙኀ ንዋየ 'much goods' (ንዋይ 'goods, equipment', accusative).

sentences.t: ወአዘዘቶሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢይኅድግዎ ፡ ህየ ፡ ለወልዳ ፡ አላ ፡ ባሕቱ ፡ ያገብርዎ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ወያግብእዎ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ይሢም ፡ መንግሥተኒ ፡ ለብሔራ ፨
sentences.l: And-she-commanded-them that not they-leave-him there, her-son, but they-hand-over(?)-him to-king and-bring-him-back to-her, and-that he-appoint kingdom-too for-her-land;
sentences.i: She commanded them not to leave her son there, but to present (?) him to the king and bring him back to her, and that the king should also establish a kingship for her land (?).
sentences.n: ወአዘዘቶሙ 'and she commanded them' (አዘዘ 'command'). ከመ ኢይኅድግዎ 'that they not leave him' (ኀደገ 'leave', + -ዎ 'him'); ለወልዳ 'her son' (ለ- the object marker again, as with ለተምሪን; ወልድ + -ኣ 'her'). አላ ባሕቱ 'but rather'. ያገብርዎ ለንጉሥ: አግበረ in the sense 'present, hand over' is a guess (?); the usual sense 'compel, subject' fits badly, so the text may be corrupt here. ወያግብእዎ ኀቤሃ 'and bring him back to her' (አግብአ + ኀበ 'to' + -ሃ 'her'). ወከመ ይሢም 'and that he appoint' (ሠየመ 'appoint'), subject unstated: I take it as Solomon, who in the story later anoints the boy (?). መንግሥተኒ 'a kingdom also'; the paragraph ends with ፨, which I read as a unit mark, not a full stop of the speech. The sense may be that Solomon is to appoint a kingship for her land (?), which would set up the law of succession in the next unit.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ሥርዐታ ፡ ለብሔረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ትነግሥ ፡ ብእሲት ፡ ድንግል ፡ እንተ ፡ ኢያውሰበት ፡ ብእሴ ፤
sentences.l: for it-was its-ordinance, of-land-of Ethiopia: she-reigns woman virgin who not she-took-a-husband man;
sentences.i: For it was the custom of the land of Ethiopia that a virgin woman should reign, one who had not taken a husband;
sentences.n: እስመ ኮነ ሥርዐታ ለብሔረ ኢትዮጵያ 'for it was the custom of the land of Ethiopia': ሥርዐት 'order, custom, ordinance'; the suffix -ኣ is the anticipatory pronoun before the ለ- genitive ('its ordinance, that of the land of Ethiopia'), as in መጋቢሃ ... ለኵሉ ብሔረ ጋዛ in unit 17. ትነግሥ ብእሲት ድንግል 'a virgin woman reigns' (ነግሠ 'reign', 3rd feminine imperfect; a bare imperfect after ኮነ ሥርዐታ gives 'that she should reign'). እንተ ኢያውሰበት ብእሴ 'who did not take a husband' (እንተ 'who' feminine relative; ኢያውሰበት: አውሰበ is said of the man 'taking a wife', so this use for a woman 'taking' a husband is unusual (?); ብእሴ 'a man', accusative). This is the book's account of a custom of a virgin queen, which the Queen is now about to change.

sentences.t: ወትቤ ፡ እምይእዘሰአ ፡ ይንገሥአ ፡ ተባዕትአ ፡ እምዘመድከአ ፡ ወኢትንገሥአ ፡ ብእሲትአ ፡ ለዓለምአ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ዘመድከአ ፡ ወዘርኡ ፡ ለትውልደ ፡ ትውልድ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said: From-now(?) let-reign male from-your-kin and-not let-reign woman for-ever, apart-from this your-kin and-his-seed for generation-of generation;
sentences.i: And she said: "From now on let a male of your kin reign, and let no woman ever reign, but only this kinsman of yours and his offspring, from generation to generation;
sentences.n: The unit is the Queen's message (to Solomon, I take it: 'your kin' = Solomon's line (?)). Orthography: the words ይእዘሰአ, ይንገሥአ, ተባዕትአ, ዘመድከአ (twice), ብእሲትአ and ዓለምአ all end in an unexplained extra አ; I cannot explain it; I treat it as a scribal or printing mark with no bearing on the translation, and translate the stems (እምይእዘሰ 'from now indeed': እም- 'from' + ይእዘ, Bezold's spelling of ይእዜ 'now', + -ሰ; ይንገሥ 'let him reign', jussive; ተባዕት 'male'; ዘመድ 'kin, relative' + -ከ 'your'; ብእሲት 'woman'; ዓለም 'eternity, world'; ለዓለም 'forever'). ዘእንበለ ዝንቱ ዘመድከ is awkward: ዘእንበለ 'apart from, except' followed by 'this your kinsman' suggests 'let none reign except this one and his seed', but the syntax joins loosely to the previous clause, so the exact sense is a little uncertain (?). ለትውልደ ትውልድ 'for generation of generation' (a common idiom of unending time).

sentences.t: ወትልክኣ ፡ ኀበ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ ጦማር ፡ ውስተ ፡ መጽሐፈ ፡ ነቢያቲሆሙ ፡ ዘብርት ፡ ወታነብራ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘተሐንጽ ፡ ለተዝካር ፡ ወለትንቢት ፡ ለደኃሪ ፡ መዋዕል ፤
sentences.l: and-you-send/write(?)-it into book-of scroll, within book-of their-prophets, the ብርት (?), and-you-place-it within house-of God which was-built for-memorial and-for-prophecy for-last days;
sentences.i: and have it written (?) in a scroll, within the book of their prophets, the one of ብርት (?), and set it in the house of God which was built as a memorial and as prophecy for the last days;
sentences.n: Corrupt or obscure in several words. ወትልክኣ: the verb is ትልክ- with a stray -ኣ; it may be ትልእክ- 'you send' (ለአከ) + -ኣ 'it' with the ክ and እ transposed, which gives 'send it to a scroll'; a verb ልከአ 'inscribe, write' I cannot confirm, so the English 'have it written' is only a guess (?). ኀበ መጽሐፈ ጦማር 'into a book, a scroll' (መጽሐፍ 'book, writing', ጦማር 'scroll, roll'). ውስተ መጽሐፈ ነቢያቲሆሙ 'within the book of their prophets'. ዘብርት 'which is of ብርት' is uncertain: ብርት may mean 'metal/bronze' or be a form of 'bright' (?); I have left it in Geʿez. ወታነብራ 'and you place it' (አንበረ 'place', + -ኣ). ቤተ እግዚኣብሔር 'the house of God' is the Jerusalem Temple (1 Kings 6). ዘተሐንጽ 'which was built' (ተሐነጸ passive of ሐነጸ 'build'; the spelling is shortened, final ጽ). ለተዝካር ወለትንቢት 'for a memorial and for prophecy' (ተዝካር 'memorial', ትንቢት 'prophecy'), ለደኃሪ መዋዕል 'for the last days' (ደኃሪ 'latter'; compare the 'last days' of the prophets).

sentences.t: ወከመ ፡ ኢይስግዱ ፡ ለፀሐይ ፡ ወለሰርጐ ፡ ሰማይ ፡ ወኢለአድባር ፡ ወአዕዋም ፡ ወኢለአእባን ፡ ወለዕፀወ ፡ ገዳም ፡ ወኢለቀላያት ፡ ወለዘ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ማይ ፡ ወኢለግልፈዋት ፡ ወአምሳለ ፡ ወርቅ ፡ ወኢለአዕዋፍ ፡ ዘይሰርር ፡ ወኢይጠየሩ ፡ ቦሙ ፡ ወኢያምልክዎሙ ፤
sentences.l: and-that not they-bow-down to-sun and-to-adornment-of heaven, nor-to-mountains and-trees, nor-to-stones and-to-trees-of wilderness, nor-to-seas and-to-what within water, nor-to-carved-images and-likenesses-of gold, nor-to-birds which flies, and-not they-take-omens(?) by-them and-not they-worship-them;
sentences.i: and that they should not bow down to the sun or to the adornment of heaven (the stars), or to mountains and trees, or to stones and the trees of the wilderness, or to seas and what is in the water, or to carved images and golden likenesses, or to birds that fly, nor practice divination (?) by them, nor worship them;
sentences.n: This clause (ከመ ኢይስግዱ 'that they not bow down', ሰገደ 'bow, prostrate') is part of the Queen's decree: the prohibition of idolatry echoes Deuteronomy 4:15–19 and the second commandment (Exodus 20:4–5). Each ወኢለ- is 'nor to' (ለ- 'to' with ሰገደ). ወኢለአድባር 'nor to mountains' (አድባር plural of ደብር), ወአዕዋም 'and trees' (አዕዋም, uncertain (?)), ወኢለአእባን 'nor to stones' (አእባን plural of እብን). ሰርጐ ሰማይ: ሰርጕ 'ornament', so 'the adornment of the heavens', the stars. ዕፀወ ገዳም 'trees of the wilderness'. ቀላያት 'seas, depths'. ወለዘ ውስተ ማይ 'and to what is in the water' (ዘ 'that which'). ግልፈዋት 'carved images' (plural of ግልፈት 'engraving') (?). አምሳለ ወርቅ 'likeness of gold'. ኢለአዕዋፍ ዘይሰርር 'nor to birds which fly' (ዘይሰርር singular for the collective; ሰረረ here 'fly', as 'sped' in ch. 31). ወኢይጠየሩ ቦሙ: ጠየረ I remember from Dillmann as 'take omens' (from birds), which fits, but I could not check it here; but the plain sense 'turn to/ look to them' is also possible (?). ወኢያምልክዎሙ 'and not make gods of them, worship them' (አምለከ). The long list is an accumulation of parallel phrases with ወኢ- and ወ-.

sentences.t: ወትንበርአ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ሥርዐት ፡ ለዓለም ፡ ወለእመቦ ፡ ዘተዐደወ ፡ እምዛቲ ፡ ሥርዐት ፡ ለይኰንኖ ፡ ዘርእከ ፡ ለዝሉፉ ።
sentences.l: And-it-will-remain this ordinance for-ever, and-if-there-is one-who transgressed from this ordinance, let-judge-him your-seed, for-[zəluf].
sentences.i: This ordinance shall stand forever; and if anyone transgresses it, let your offspring judge him, for good (?).
sentences.n: ወትንበርአ ዛቲ ሥርዐት 'and this ordinance shall remain' (ነበረ 'remain, sit', 3rd feminine imperfect; ዛቲ 'this', feminine; the final -አ again as in unit 7). ወለእመቦ ዘተዐደወ 'and if there is one who transgressed' (ለእመ + ቦ 'there is'; ተዐደወ 'transgress, overstep'). ለይኰንኖ 'let him judge him' (ኰነነ 'judge', jussive with ለ-). ዘርእከ is 'your seed' (ዘርእ + -ከ). ለዝሉፉ is unclear; in ch. 24 (ወይእቲ ትከውነኒ ለዝሉፉ) it stands as an adverbial phrase, and I follow that: perhaps 'for good, continually' (related to ዘልፈ) (?).

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ ሀበነ ፡ እምዘፈረ ፡ ልብሳ ፡ ዘንኤምኃ ፡ ለጽዮን ፡ ቅድስት ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: But give-us from-edge(?)-of her-garment ዘንኤምኃ (?) for-Zion holy heavenly, ark-of his-law of-God;
sentences.i: But give us, from the edge (?) of her garment, the ዘንኤምኃ (?) for Zion, the holy, heavenly Ark of God's law;
sentences.n: A hard unit; the sense is a request to Solomon: ወባሕቱ ሀበነ 'but give us' (ሀበ 'give', imperative + -ነ 'us'). እምዘፈረ ልብሳ: እም- 'from', ልብስ 'garment' + -ኣ 'her' (Zion is feminine). ዘፈረ I cannot confirm; if it is ዘፈር 'edge, fringe' (unverified) the sense 'from the border of her garment' fits a request for a relic (?). ዘንኤምኃ is not a form I can resolve, perhaps a garbled relative + noun; I leave it in transliteration (?). ለጽዮን 'for Zion' (ጽዮን 'Zion'). ቅድስት ሰማያዊት 'holy, heavenly' (feminine adjectives). ታቦተ ሕጉ ለእግዚኣብሔር 'the Ark of His law, of God': the Kebra Nagast identifies Zion with the Ark of the Covenant (ታቦት), earthly copy of a heavenly Zion; the request for a relic of Zion anticipates the Ark theme of the coming chapters. The reading of the whole unit is conjectural.

sentences.t: ሰላም ፡ ለጽንዐ ፡ መንግሣትከ ፡ ወለጥበብከ ፡ ብርህት ፡ ዘወሀበከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ፈጣሪነ ፨
sentences.l: Peace to-firmness-of your-kingdom and-to-your-wisdom bright which gave-you God, God-of Israel our-creator. ፨
sentences.i: Peace to the strength of your kingdom, and to your radiant wisdom, which God gave you, the God of Israel, our Creator." ፨
sentences.n: ሰላም ለ- 'peace to' is a salutation formula of letters; here it closes the Queen's message. ጽንዐ መንግሣትከ 'the firmness (ጽንዕ) of your kingdom' (construct chain, + -ከ 'your'); ጥበብከ ብርህት 'your bright wisdom' (ብርህት feminine adjective agreeing with ጥበብ). ዘወሀበከ 'which he gave you' (ወሀበ + -ከ). አምላከ እስራኤል 'God of Israel', ፈጣሪነ 'our creator' (ፈጣሪ + -ነ). The unit ends in ፨, which marks a pause, not the end of the chapter.

sentences.t: ወአግሐሠቶ ፡ እንተ ፡ ባሕቲቱ ፡ ወወሀበቶ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ትእምርተ ፡ ዘወሀባ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ዘውስተ ፡ አጽባዕቱ ፡ ሕልቀተ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያእምሮ ፡ ለወልዲ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ይዘከር ፡ ነገራ ፡ ወኪዳና ፡ ዘተካየደት ፡ በኵሉ ፡ መዋዕለ ፡ ሕይወታ ፡ ከመ ፡ ታምልኮ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ወእለ ፡ እምታሕተ ፡ መንግሣታ ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ዘወሀባ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ።
sentences.l: And-she-drew-aside-him, which his-solitude, and-she-gave-him, she, sign which gave-her Solomon, which within his-fingers ring, that he-know my-son and-that he-remember her-word and-her-covenant which she-covenanted in-all days-of her-life, that she-worship God, she and-those who under her-kingdom, in-all what gave-her God.
sentences.i: She took him aside, alone, and she gave him the sign that Solomon had given her, the ring from his fingers, so that Solomon might know my son and remember her word and the covenant she had made all the days of her life, to worship God, she and those under her rule, in all that God had given her.
sentences.n: ወአግሐሠቶ 'and she drew him aside' (the Queen is the subject, the boy the object; as in ch. 31, አግሐሠ). እንተ ባሕቲቱ 'by himself, alone' (the idiom of ch. 31; ባሕቲት 'solitude' + -ሁ). ወወሀበቶ ይእቲ 'and she, she gave him' (ይእቲ 'she' emphasizes the subject). ትእምርተ ዘወሀባ ሰሎሞን 'a sign which Solomon gave her' (the ring of ch. 31; ዘወሀባ is ዘ + ወሀበ + -ኣ). ሕልቀተ 'ring' in apposition. ከመ ያእምሮ ለወልዲ: ከመ + subjunctive 'that he may know' (አእመረ; the final -ኦ of ያእምሮ is 'him', anticipating ለወልዲ: 'that he know him, my son'), ወልዲ 'my son' (the Queen speaks in the first person here, a lapse from the narrative into her words; ወልድየ would be usual, ወልዲ is a variant or slip (?)). ወከመ ይዘከር 'and that he remember' (ተዘከረ 'remember', a passive-reflexive stem). ነገራ ወኪዳና 'her word and her covenant' (ኪዳን 'covenant'). ዘተካየደት 'which she covenanted' (ተካየደ 'make a covenant (with another)'). በኵሉ መዋዕለ ሕይወታ 'in all the days of her life'. ከመ ታምልኮ 'that she worship him, make him her god' (አምለከ). ወእለ እምታሕተ መንግሣታ 'and those under her rule' (እምታሕተ 'from under', i.e. 'subject to'). በኵሉ ዘወሀባ እግዚኣብሔር 'in all that God gave her'. The unit, at 32 words, is long but kept whole, since it has no ፤.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ፈነወቶ ፡ በሰላም ፤
sentences.l: And-then she-sent-him in-peace;
sentences.i: Then she sent him away in peace;
sentences.n: ወእምዝ 'and after this, then' (እም- 'from' + ዝ 'this'). ፈነወቶ 'she sent him off' (ፈነወ + -ቶ 'him'). በሰላም 'in peace', a farewell formula.

sentences.t: ወአርትዑ ፡ ፍኖተ ፡ ወሖሩ ፡ ወበጽሑ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ደወለ ፡ ጋዛ ፤
sentences.l: and-they-made-straight road and-went and-arrived into land-of region-of Gaza;
sentences.i: and they went straight along the road, travelled on, and reached the land of the region of Gaza;
sentences.n: ወአርትዑ ፍኖተ 'and they made the road straight' (አርትዐ 'make straight, set right'; the idiom is of travelling directly). ወሖሩ ወበጽሑ 'and they went and arrived' (ሖረ, በጽሐ). ብሔረ ደወለ ጋዛ: ደወል is not secure; as 'region, border-district' (a 'border, boundary' sense, which I could not check) it gives 'the land of the borders of Gaza' (?). Gaza (ጋዛ) was a city on the road between Jerusalem and Egypt, and the boy's party reached it on the way south to Ethiopia.

sentences.t: ወይእቲ ፡ ሀገር ፡ ዘወሀባ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ለንግሣተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፤
sentences.l: and that city which gave-it Solomon king to-queen(?)-of Ethiopia;
sentences.i: and this city was one that King Solomon had given to the queen (?) of Ethiopia;
sentences.n: ወይእቲ ሀገር 'and that city' (ይእቲ is the feminine 'that, she'; ሀገር is feminine here). ዘወሀባ ሰሎሞን ንጉሥ 'which Solomon the king gave it' (ዘ- + ወሀበ + -ኣ 'it/her'). ለንግሣተ ኢትዮጵያ: I read ንግሣተ as ንግሥተ 'queen of' (spelled with ሣ as መንግሣት is for መንግሥት), the same word as ለንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ in unit 39 and ለንግሥተ ህንደኬ in the next unit, so 'to the queen of Ethiopia', that is, to Makeda (?); 'to the kingdom of Ethiopia' (ንግሣት as a variant of መንግሥት) is the other possibility (?). The claim that Solomon gave Gaza to Ethiopia is the chronicle's own, set up to link with the next unit's use of Acts 8.

sentences.t: ወበውስተ ፡ ግብረ ፡ ሐዋርያትሂ ፡ ጸሐፈ ፡ ሉቃስ ፡ ወንጌላዊ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ መጋቢሃ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ለኵሉ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ጋዛ ፡ ኅጽዋ ፡ ለንግሥተ ፡ ህንደኬ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዘአምነ ፡ በቃለ ፡ ሉቃስ ፡ ሐዋርያ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-within acts-of apostles-also wrote Luke evangelist, saying: steward-of-it is he for-all land-of Gaza, her-eunuch(?), of-queen-of Candace, he who believed by-word-of Luke apostle. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: And in the Acts of the Apostles too, Luke the evangelist wrote, saying: he was its steward over all the land of Gaza, the eunuch (?) of the Queen of Candace; he is the one who believed through the word of Luke the apostle. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.n: The allusion is to Acts 8:26–40: Philip meets, on the road toward Gaza, an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of 'Candace, queen of the Ethiopians', 'in charge of all her treasure' (Acts 8:27); he is baptized. As I remember the Geʿez Bible (unchecked), the word 'treasure' there is ጋዛ, the same letters as the city's name, and the Kebra Nagast reads it as the place Gaza (that is how it makes the official governor of 'all the land of Gaza' and Gaza Ethiopian). ወበውስተ ግብረ ሐዋርያትሂ 'and in the Acts of the Apostles too' (ግብር 'deed', -ሂ 'also'). ጸሐፈ ሉቃስ ወንጌላዊ 'Luke the evangelist wrote' (Luke is the traditional author of Acts). እንዘ ይብል 'saying'. መጋቢሃ ውእቱ 'he is its steward' (መጋቢ 'steward, manager'). ኅጽዋ 'eunuch': I take it as ኅጽው 'eunuch' (from memory of Dillmann; unchecked) with the final ዋ as ኅጽው + the 3rd feminine suffix -ኣ ('her'), anticipating ለንግሥተ ህንደኬ, the same construction as መጋቢሃ ... ለኵሉ ብሔረ ጋዛ. ንግሥተ ህንደኬ 'the queen of Candace' (Candace, ህንደኬ, is really a title of Meroitic queens, treated here as a name). ዘአምነ በቃለ ሉቃስ 'who believed through the word of Luke' (አምነ 'believe'). The text credits Luke's word, not Philip's, for the eunuch's belief; in Acts it is Philip who preaches to and baptizes him. The seven ፨ close chapter 33 and stay with the final unit.

sentences.t: ፴፬ ፡ ዘከመ ፡ በጽሐ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ እሙ ።
sentences.l: 34. How he-arrived land-of his-mother.
sentences.i: Chapter 34: How He Reached His Mother's Land
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፴፬ is 34 (spoken ሠላሳ ወአርባዕቱ, śälasa wä-ʾärbaʿtu). ዘከመ 'how'; በጽሐ 'he arrived' (በጽሐ takes a direct object of the place, ብሔረ 'the land of'); እሙ 'his mother' (እም 'mother' + -ሁ, written -ሙ). The 'mother's land' is presumably Gaza, reached as Ethiopian territory (?); the next unit says ሀገረ እሙ 'the city of his mother'.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ በጽሐ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ እሙ ፡ ተፈሥሐ ፡ በህየ ፡ በክብር ፡ ወበአምኃ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-arrived city-of his-mother he-rejoiced there in-honor and-in-gift;
sentences.i: When he reached his mother's city he rejoiced there, in honor and with gifts;
sentences.n: ወሶበ በጽሐ 'and when he arrived' (ሶበ 'when' + perfect). ሀገረ እሙ 'the city of his mother', presumably the same place, Gaza (?), where he is welcomed. ተፈሥሐ 'he rejoiced' (ተፈሥሐ). በህየ 'there'. በክብር ወበአምኃ 'in honor and in gifts'. It is unclear whether he rejoices at being honored or is honored by others; the sentence has only 'he rejoiced'.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ርእይዎ ፡ መሰሎሙ ፡ ፍጹመ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወሰገዲ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ባሕ ፡ ሕየው ፡ አበ ፡ ነጋሢ ፡ ወያበውኡ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ አምኃ ፡ ወጋዳ ፡ ወመጋዝአ ፡ ወምሳሓተ ፡ ከመ ፡ ንጉሦሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-when they-saw-him, it-seemed-to-them perfectly (that he was) Solomon king, and-they-bowed to-him and-said-to-him: Bah(?) live, father-of king, and-they-bring to-him gift and-gada (?) and-treasure(?) and-feast(?) as their-king;
sentences.i: When they saw him, he seemed to them in every way King Solomon, and they bowed to him and said to him: "Live, father of the king (?)," and they brought him gifts, and gada (?), and treasures (?), and banquets (?), as to their king;
sentences.n: ወሶበ ርእይዎ 'and when they saw him' (ርእየ, 3rd plural, + -ዎ). መሰሎሙ 'it seemed to them' (መሰለ 'be like, seem' with the dative suffix -ሙ 'to them'); ፍጹመ 'wholly, perfectly' (accusative of ፍጹም 'perfect'). The point: everyone takes the boy for Solomon. ሰገዲ ሎቱ 'they bowed to him' (ሰገዲ is a spelling of 3rd plural ሰገዱ, or an unmarked variant). ባሕ ሕየው አበ ነጋሢ: ባሕ I cannot place, perhaps a cry of greeting (?), and the English leaves it unrendered; ሕየው 'live!' (imperative of ሐይወ, in the ancient royal greeting 'live'); አበ ነጋሢ 'father of the king': ነጋሢ is an agent-noun 'one who reigns'; 'father of the king' addressed to Solomon makes sense (he is Menelik's father) but is not an obvious greeting for a stranger taken to be Solomon; so the whole is uncertain (?). ያበውኡ 'they bring' (አብአ 'bring in', causative of ቦአ; imperfect ያበውእ). አምኃ 'gift'. ጋዳ and መጋዝ (the printed form is መጋዝአ, with the stray final አ, see ch. 33, unit 7) and ምሳሓተ: I cannot place ጋዳ (?) (it may be a misprint of ጋዛ 'treasure', the word of Acts 8:27 discussed in the note to ch. 33, unit 17) (?); መጋዝ is 'storehouse, treasure' (?) (cf. ጋዛ 'treasure' in the previous chapter); ምሳሓተ is 'meals, feasts' (ምሳሕ 'meal, feast') (?). Together: tribute of goods, stores and banquets. ከመ ንጉሦሙ 'as their king' (ንጉሥ + -ሙ).

sentences.t: ወተሀውከት ፡ ኵላ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ጋዛ ፡ እስከ ፡ ደወለ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብሉ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ።
sentences.l: And-was-stirred all land-of Gaza as-far-as region-of Judah, saying: This is he king Solomon.
sentences.i: All the land of Gaza was stirred as far as the region of Judah, and they said: "This is King Solomon."
sentences.n: ወተሀውከት 'and it was stirred, thrown into commotion' (ተሀውከ 'be disturbed', feminine; its subject ብሔር, 'land', is treated as feminine). ኵላ ብሔረ ጋዛ 'the whole land of Gaza' (ኵላ is the feminine form, 'all'). እስከ ደወለ ይሁዳ 'as far as the region of Judah' (see ch. 33 for ደወል). እንዘ ይብሉ 'saying' (circumstantial plural). ዝንቱ ውእቱ 'this is he' (identifying the boy with the king).

sentences.t: ወቦ ፡ ዘይቤ ፡ ንጉሥሰ ፡ ሀለወ ፡ በኢየሩሳሌም ፡ የሐንጽ ፡ ቤቶ ፤
sentences.l: And-there-is one-who said: The-king indeed is in-Jerusalem, building his-house;
sentences.i: Some said: "The king is in Jerusalem, building his house;
sentences.n: ወቦ ዘይቤ 'and there is one who said' (ቦ 'there is' + ዘ 'who' + ይቤ). ንጉሥሰ 'the king indeed' (-ሰ 'indeed, as for'). ሀለወ 'is' (ሀሎ). በኢየሩሳሌም 'in Jerusalem'. የሐንጽ ቤቶ 'is building his house' (ሐነጸ 'build', imperfect; ቤቶ is a spelling of ቤቱ). I take 'his house' as Solomon's own palace (1 Kings 7:1) (?), contrasting with the Temple in the next unit.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ፈጸመ ፡ ሐኒጸ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: for he-finished building house-of God;
sentences.i: for he had finished building the house of God;"
sentences.n: እስመ ፈጸመ ሐኒጸ 'for he finished building' (ፈጸመ 'complete' + infinitive ሐኒጸ in the accusative, from ሐነጸ). ቤተ እግዚኣብሔር 'the house of God', i.e. the Temple (1 Kings 6:38; 7:1). The two units together reflect the biblical order: the Temple first (seven years), then his own house (thirteen years).

sentences.t: ወቦ ፡ እለ ፡ ይቤሉ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዳዊት ።
sentences.l: and-there-are those-who said: This is Solomon king, son-of David.
sentences.i: and others said: "This is King Solomon, the son of David."
sentences.n: ወቦ እለ ይቤሉ 'and there are those who said' (እለ is the plural relative; ይቤሉ 'they said'). ሰሎሞን ንጉሥ ወልደ ዳዊት 'Solomon the king, son of David' (ወልደ is the construct of ወልድ). The people of Gaza are divided into two opinions about whether this is Solomon.

sentences.t: ወተሀውኩ ፡ ወተጋአዙ ፡ ወፈነዉ ፡ መባርዲን ፤
sentences.l: And-they-were-troubled and-hurried(?) and-sent mäbardin;
sentences.i: They were troubled and hurried (?), and sent mounted couriers (?);
sentences.n: ወተሀውኩ 'and they were troubled' (ተሀውከ, 3rd plural). ወተጋአዙ is uncertain: ተጋአዘ I take as 'hurry, be restless' (?). ወፈነዉ 'and they sent' (ፈነወ; the printed ፈነዉ is the 3rd plural). መባርዲን is an unusual word: it is explained by the next unit ሰብአ አፍራስ 'horsemen', and I take it as a loan from Arabic barīd 'mounted courier, post' (?); I leave it in transliteration (mäbardin) in the interlinear and say 'mounted couriers' in the English.

sentences.t: ሰብአ ፡ አፍራስ ፤
sentences.l: men-of horses;
sentences.i: horsemen,
sentences.n: ሰብአ አፍራስ 'men of horses, horsemen' (ሰብእ 'man' in the construct plural ሰብአ; አፍራስ plural of ፈረስ 'horse'), in apposition to መባርዲን: it glosses the odd word of the previous unit. The ፤ cuts a one-phrase unit in Bezold's punctuation, so it is kept as its own unit.

sentences.t: እለ ፡ የኀሥሥዎ ፡ ለንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ እመ ፡ ጥዩቀ ፡ ህየ ፡ ሀሎ ፡ ወእመ ፡ ሀሎ ፡ ምስሌሆሙ ።
sentences.l: who seek king Solomon, whether truly there he-was and-whether he-was with-them.
sentences.i: who were to find out whether King Solomon was truly there, or whether he was with them.
sentences.n: እለ የኀሥሥዎ 'who seek him' (ኀሠሠ 'seek', imperfect 3rd plural + -ዎ 'him'; ለንጉሥ ሰሎሞን the object marked with ለ-). እመ ... ወእመ ... 'whether ... or whether' (እመ 'if, whether'). ጥዩቀ 'exactly, truly' (ጥዩቅ 'certain', accusative as adverb). ህየ ሀሎ 'he was there' (that is, in Jerusalem); ምስሌሆሙ 'with them', i.e. in the Ethiopian party. The English 'to find out' is implied by the whole clause.

sentences.t: ወበጽሑ ፡ መባርዲን ፡ ዐቀብተ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ወረከብዎ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ህየ ፡ ወሰገዲ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-arrived the-mäbardin, guards-of city-of Jerusalem, and-found Solomon king there, and-bowed to-him and-said-to-him;
sentences.i: The couriers, guardians of the city of Jerusalem, came and found King Solomon there, and bowed to him and said to him:
sentences.n: ወበጽሑ መባርዲን 'and the couriers arrived'. ዐቀብተ ሀገረ ኢየሩሳሌም 'the guards of the city of Jerusalem' (ዐቃቢ 'guard', plural ዐቀብት in the construct). Whether the same men sent from Gaza are being called 'guards' (perhaps because they served as sentries), or a different body of the city's own, is not clear (?). Another reading takes ዐቀብተ as the object of በጽሑ (በጽሐ takes a direct object): 'the couriers reached the guards of the city of Jerusalem and found Solomon there' (?). ወረከብዎ 'and they found him' (ረከበ); ወሰገዲ ሎቱ as in unit 20 (the printed 3rd plural spelling again). ወይቤልዎ 'and they said to him' (ይቤ + -ልዎ 'to him').

sentences.t: ባሕ ፡ ሕየው ፡ አበ ፡ ነጋሢ ፡ ሀገርሰ ፡ ተሀውከት ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘመጽአ ፡ ፩ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ዘይመስል ፡ አርአያከ ፡ ወአምሳሊከ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሕፀት ፡ ወብዕድና ፤
sentences.l: Bah(?), live, father-of king! The-city indeed was-stirred on-account-of he-who came, one merchant who resembles your-form and-your-likeness without lack and-difference;
sentences.i: "Live, father of the king (?)! The city has been stirred up because of a merchant who has come, who resembles your form and your likeness without any lack or difference;
sentences.n: ባሕ ሕየው አበ ነጋሢ repeats the greeting of unit 20; ባሕ is not understood (?). ሀገርሰ ተሀውከት 'the city indeed was stirred' (ሀገር feminine). በእንተ ዘመጽአ ፩ ነጋዲ 'on account of one merchant who came' (በእንተ 'because of', ዘመጽአ 'he who came'); ፩ is 1 (spoken አሐዱ, ʾäḥädu) and ነጋዲ 'merchant', the boy being taken as a merchant of the caravan. ዘይመስል አርአያከ ወአምሳሊከ 'who resembles your form and your likeness' (መሰለ takes an accusative: አርአያ 'appearance, form', አምሳል 'likeness', + -ከ 'your'); which recalls the wording of Genesis 1:26 'our image and likeness' (as I remember the Geʿez Genesis, unchecked). ዘእንበለ ሕፀት ወብዕድና 'without lack and difference' (ሕፀት 'lack, defect', ብዕድና 'otherness, difference'). The speakers call the boy a merchant, presumably as one of the caravan (?).

sentences.t: ኪያከ ፡ ይመስል ፡ በጸዳል ፡ ወበሥን ፡ በቆም ፡ ወበኅይስና ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ጥልቀት ፡ ወተባዕዶ ፤
sentences.l: You he-resembles in-radiance and-in-beauty, in-stature and-in-excellence(?), without defect(?) and-difference;
sentences.i: he resembles you in radiance and beauty, in stature and in excellence (?), without any defect (?) or difference;
sentences.n: ኪያከ ይመስል 'he resembles you' (ኪያከ the independent accusative 'you', put first for emphasis, as object of ይመስል). በጸዳል 'in brightness, radiance'; ወበሥን 'and in beauty'; በቆም 'in stature'; ወበኅይስና: ኅይስና 'goodness, excellence' (from ኀየሰ 'be good, excel'; so glossed, with a query, in ch. 27) (?). ዘእንበለ ጥልቀት ወተባዕዶ: ጥልቀት I take as 'defect, fault' on the pattern of ሕፀት in the previous unit, but the form is not secure (?); ተባዕዶ 'difference, otherness' (infinitive of ተባዕደ). The nouns are in a short chain, each introduced by በ- 'in, with'.

sentences.t: አዕይንቲሁ ፡ ፍሡሓት ፡ ከመዘ ፡ ሰክረ ፡ ወይነ ፡ ወአቊያጺሁኒ ፡ ቈጢጣን ፡ ወማኅፈደ ፡ ክሳዲኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ማኅፈደ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ አቡከ ፡ ወኪያከ ፡ ይመስል ፡ በኵሉ ፡ ፍጹም ፡ አባል ፡ ዘይትማሰለከ ፨
sentences.l: his-eyes bright like-one drunk with-wine, and-his-brows-too arched(?), and-the-tower(?)-of his-neck-too like tower(?)-of David your-father, and you he-resembles in-every perfect limb which is-compared-to-you. ፨
sentences.i: his eyes are bright as if drunk with wine, and his brows (?) arched (?), and the tower (?) of his neck, too, like the tower of David your father; and he resembles you in every perfect limb, each matching yours."
sentences.n: አዕይንቲሁ ፍሡሓት 'his eyes are glad, bright' (ፍሡሕ 'glad'; feminine plural to agree with the 'eyes'). ከመዘ ሰክረ ወይነ: ከመ + ዘ 'like one who', ሰክረ 'was drunk', ወይነ the accusative of the wine (an accusative of means); the comparison is of shining eyes. ወአቊያጺሁኒ ቈጢጣን: አቊያጺሁ was glossed in ch. 31 as 'his brows (or eyelids)' (?), and I keep that; ቈጢጣን I take as 'arched' (?) from a root of bending, but cannot confirm it. ወማኅፈደ ክሳዲኒ: ማኅፈድ is 'tower' (Dillmann, from memory, unchecked), so 'the tower of his neck, too', a neck like a tower, which recalls Song of Songs 4:4 ('your neck is like the tower of David') and suits 'like the tower of David your father'. In ch. 31 the same word was given as 'stature or frame (?)'; that is the figurative sense of 'tower' as the build of the body, and the query stays (?). ክሳድ 'neck' (the ending ክሳዲ- + ኒ, for the expected ክሳዱኒ 'his neck too', is unexplained (?)). ከመ ማኅፈደ ዳዊት አቡከ 'like that of David your father' (ዳዊት አቡከ, with -ከ 'your'). ዘይትማሰለከ 'which matches you' (ተማሰለ 'be like one another, be compared' + -ከ). The unit ends in ፨, kept as a unit mark.

sentences.t: አውሥአ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ወይቤሎሙ ፡ አይቴኬ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ይፈቅድ ፡ ሐዊረ ።
sentences.l: Answered king and-said-to-them: Where-then does-he wish to-go?
sentences.i: The king answered and said to them: "And where does he wish to go?"
sentences.n: አውሥአ ንጉሥ 'the king answered' (አውሥአ, the regular verb 'answer', followed by ወይቤሎሙ 'and said to them'). አይቴኬ 'where then?' (አይቴ 'where' + the enclitic -ኬ, 'then, now'). ይፈቅድ ሐዊረ 'he wishes to go' (ፈቀደ 'wish' + infinitive ሐዊረ, from ሖረ). Solomon is the real king, in Jerusalem, hearing of the look-alike for the first time.

sentences.t: አውሥኡ ፡ ወይቤልዎ ፡ ለሊሁሰ ፡ ኢሐተትናሁ ፡ እስመ ፡ ግሩም ፡ ከማከ ፤
sentences.l: They-answered and-said-to-him: He-himself indeed we-did-not-ask-him, for he awesome like-you;
sentences.i: They answered and said to him: "We did not question him himself, for he is awe-inspiring like you;
sentences.n: ለሊሁሰ 'he himself indeed' (ለሊሁ 'himself' + -ሰ). ኢሐተትናሁ 'we did not ask him' (ሐተተ 'inquire, ask'; 1st plural + -ሁ 'him'). እስመ ግሩም ከማከ 'for he is awesome like you' (ግሩም 'awe-inspiring, fearsome'; ከማከ 'like you'). The couriers excuse themselves for not questioning the stranger: his bearing, like the king's, perhaps kept them at a distance.

sentences.t: ወእሊአሁሰ ፡ ይቤሉ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ተስእልናሆሙ ፡ ወንቤሎሙ ፡ እምአይቴ ፡ መጻእክሙ ፡ ወአይቴ ፡ ተሐውሩ ፡ ወይቤሉነ ፡ መጻእነ ፡ እምአድያመ ፡ ህንደኬ ፡ ወኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወነሐውር ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ይሁዳ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ።
sentences.l: and-his-people indeed said when we-asked-them, and-we-said-to-them: From-where did-you-come and-where do-you-go, and-they-said-to-us: We-came from the-regions-of Candace and-Ethiopia, and-we-go land-of Judah to Solomon king.
sentences.i: but his companions, when we asked them and said to them, 'Where have you come from and where are you going?', said to us: 'We have come from the regions of Candace and Ethiopia, and we are going to the land of Judah, to King Solomon.'"
sentences.n: ወእሊአሁሰ 'and his own people indeed' (እሊአሁ 'those of his, his men'; the -ሰ marks the contrast with the traveler himself). ሶበ ተስእልናሆሙ 'when we asked them' (ተስእለ 'ask', 1st plural + -ሆሙ 'them'). ወንቤሎሙ 'and we said to them' (ንቤሎሙ is 1st plural, 'we said'). እምአይቴ መጻእክሙ 'from where have you come' (መጻእክሙ 2nd plural); ወአይቴ ተሐውሩ 'and where do you go'. ወይቤሉነ 'and they said to us' (ይቤሉ + -ነ). መጻእነ እምአድያመ ህንደኬ ወኢትዮጵያ 'we came from the borders of Candace and Ethiopia' (አድያም 'borders, regions', construct plural), ወነሐውር 'and we go'; ኀበ ሰሎሞን ንጉሥ 'to King Solomon'. The unit holds two nested quotations.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ሰምዐ ፡ ዘንተ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ተሀውከ ፡ ልቡ ፡ ወተሐሠየ ፡ በመንፈሱ ፡ እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ውሉደ ፡ በውእቱ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሕፃን ፡ ዘ፯ ፡ ዓም ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ ኢዮርብዓም ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-heard this, Solomon king, was-troubled his-heart and-he-rejoiced(?) in-his-spirit, because there-is-not children in-that day except child of-7 years whose-name Jeroboam;
sentences.i: When King Solomon heard this, his heart was troubled and his spirit rejoiced (?), for in those days he had no sons except a child of seven years whose name was Jeroboam;
sentences.n: ተሀውከ ልቡ 'his heart was troubled' (ተሀውከ with ልብ 'heart' as subject). ወተሐሠየ በመንፈሱ 'and he rejoiced (?) in his spirit' (ተሐሠየ 'he rejoiced, was glad', from the root of ሐሤት 'joy', as ተሐሠየ is glossed in ch. 25–26; the first draft's 'was grieved' is set aside), so 'troubled in heart, glad in spirit', the gladness having its reason in the next clause (he had no grown son) (?). እስመ አልቦ ውሉደ 'for there were no children, he had no sons' (አልቦ 'there is not' + the accusative ውሉድ). ዘእንበለ ሕፃን 'except a child'. ዘ፯ ዓም: ዘ- is the relative, ፯ is 7 (spoken ሰብዐቱ, säbʿätu), and ዓም I take as a short form of ዓመት 'year' (?); 'a child of seven years' or 'who is of seven years'. ዘስሙ ኢዮርብዓም 'whose name is Jeroboam'. Jeroboam (1 Kings 11–12) is in the Bible a rebel who led the ten northern tribes against Solomon's son Rehoboam; here the text calls Solomon's only son by that name, an apparent confusion with Rehoboam (?). I translate it as printed.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ ዘከረ ፡ ጳውሎስ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ እስመ ፡ አእበዳ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለጥበበ ፡ ዝዓለም ፡ ዘመከረ ፡ በጥበቡ ።
sentences.l: As mentioned Paul and-said: for he-made-foolish-it God the-wisdom-of this-world, which counselled in-its-wisdom.
sentences.i: As Paul recalled when he said: "God has made foolish the wisdom of this world, which took counsel in its own wisdom."
sentences.n: In 1 Corinthians 1:20 Paul asks, 'Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?'; the chronicle applies it to Solomon's plan in the next unit, a wise king with a thousand wives yet only one child. በከመ ዘከረ ጳውሎስ 'as Paul mentioned' (ዘከረ 'remember, mention'). እስመ አእበዳ እግዚኣብሔር 'for God made foolish' (አእበደ, spelled for አዐበደ, the causative of ዐበደ 'be foolish', with -ኣ 'it' joined: አእበዳ). ጥበበ ዝዓለም 'the wisdom of this world' (ዝ- 'this' + ዓለም, the construct chain being ጥበበ ዓለም with a demonstrative ዝ stuck onto the second member). ዘመከረ በጥበቡ 'which took counsel in its wisdom' (መከረ 'counsel, plan'; ዘ- refers to the wisdom).

sentences.t: ወይቤ ፡ እም፲፻ ፡ አንስት ፡ እወልድ ፡ ፲፻ ፡ ተባዕተ ፡ ወእወርስ ፡ አህጉረ ፡ ፀር ፡ ወኣመዘብር ፡ ጣዖታተ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said: From 1000 women I-will-beget 1000 male, and-I-will-possess cities-of enemy and-I-will-despoil(?) idols;
sentences.i: Solomon had said: "From a thousand women I will beget a thousand sons, and I will take possession of the cities of the enemy and despoil (?) the idols;"
sentences.n: This is Solomon's earlier plan (hence 'he had said'). The numeral እም፲፻ is written without a space: እም- 'from' + ፲፻ (ten hundreds = 1000; spoken ዐሠርቱ ምእት, ʿäśärtu məʾət, literally 'ten hundreds' (a reconstruction (?))). The number matches the 700 wives and 300 concubines of 1 Kings 11:3. አንስት 'women' (plural of ብእሲት); እወልድ 'I will beget' (ወለደ); ተባዕተ 'males, sons' (accusative). ወእወርስ 'and I will inherit, take possession of' (ወረሰ), አህጉረ ፀር 'cities of the enemy' (አህጉር plural of ሀገር, ፀር 'enemy'). ወኣመዘብር: the ኣ- is the same unusual spelling of the 1st singular prefix (for እ-) as in ኣነብር below; the verb I take from መዝበረ 'plunder, lay waste' (?), so 'despoil the idols', but this is uncertain. ጣዖታተ 'idols' (accusative plural).

sentences.t: ወኢወሀቦ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ፫ ፡ ደቂቅ ፤
sentences.l: and-not-he-gave-him except 3 children;
sentences.i: but God gave him no more than three children;
sentences.n: ወኢወሀቦ 'and he did not give him' (the subject is unstated; I take it as God, from unit 36). ዘእንበለ ፫ ደቂቅ 'except three children': ፫ is 3 (spoken ሠለስቱ, śälästu) and ደቂቅ 'children, little ones'. The identity of the three is not given, and the next unit turns at once to the child who 'grows'; they do not square with the single seven-year-old child of unit 35 (?). I translate the unit as it stands.

sentences.t: ዘይልህቅ ፡ ወልዱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ወልዳ ፡ ለንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ በኵር ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ዘይቤ ፡ በትንቢት ፡ መሐለ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለዳዊት ፡ በጽድቅ ፡ ወኢይኔስሕ ፡ ከመ ፡ እምፍሬ ፡ ከርሥከ ፡ ኣነብር ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበርከ ፤
sentences.l: who grows, his-son king-of Ethiopia, son-of-her to-queen-of Ethiopia, firstborn he, which he-said in-prophecy: swore God to-David in-truth and-not he-will-repent: that from-fruit-of your-belly I-will-set on your-throne;
sentences.i: the one who grows is his son, the king of Ethiopia, the son of the Queen of Ethiopia; he is the firstborn of whom it was said in prophecy: God swore to David in truth, and will not repent, that 'from the fruit of your belly I will set one upon your throne';
sentences.n: ዘይልህቅ ወልዱ 'the one who grows is his son' (ልህቀ 'grow up'; ዘይልህቅ the grown one). ንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ 'king of Ethiopia', ወልዳ ለንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ 'her son, of the queen of Ethiopia' (ለ- is the possessive linker). በኵር ውእቱ 'he is the firstborn'. ዘይቤ በትንቢት 'which he said in prophecy' introduces the quotation of Psalm 132:11 (131:11 in the Septuagint numbering; also Psalm 89:3–4 and 2 Samuel 7:12): God's oath to David that one of his descendants would sit on his throne. መሐለ እግዚኣብሔር ለዳዊት በጽድቅ ወኢይኔስሕ 'God swore to David in truth, and will not repent' (መሐለ 'swear', ነስሐ 'repent, change one's mind', imperfect ይኔስሕ). ከመ እምፍሬ ከርሥከ ኣነብር ዲበ መንበርከ 'that from the fruit of your belly I will set (one) on your throne' (ፍሬ 'fruit', ከርሥ 'belly, womb'; ኣነብር is the 1st person imperfect with ኣ-, አንበረ 'set, place'). The chronicle reads the oath of the Psalm as pointing to Ethiopian kings too, and to Christ in the next unit.

sentences.t: ወወሀቦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ሞገሰ ፡ በቅድሜሁ ፡ ለዳዊት ፡ ገብሩ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ዘይነብር ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበረመለኮት ፡ እምዘርኡ ፡ በሥጋ ፡ እምድንግል ፡ ወይኴንን ፡ ሕያዋነ ፡ ወሙታነ ፡ ወይፈድዮ ፡ ለኵሉ ፡ በከመ ፡ ምግባሩ ፡ ዘሎቱ ፡ ይደሉ ፡ ስብሐት ፡ ለእግዚእነ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ለዓለመ ፡ ዓለም ፡ አሜን ፤
sentences.l: And-gave-him God favor before-him for-David his-servant, and-gave-him one-who sits on throne-of-divinity from-his-seed in-flesh from virgin, and-judges living-ones and-dead-ones and-repays to-everyone according-to his-deed, to-whom is-fitting glory, to-our-Lord Jesus Christ, for-age-of age, Amen;
sentences.i: God gave David his servant favor before him, and gave him one who would sit on the throne of divinity, from his seed in the flesh, from a virgin, who judges the living and the dead and repays everyone according to his deeds, to whom glory is due, to our Lord Jesus Christ, forever and ever, Amen;
sentences.n: ወወሀቦ እግዚኣብሔር ሞገሰ 'and God gave him favor' (ሞገስ 'grace, favor'; the object -ቦ 'him' is David); በቅድሜሁ 'before him'; ለዳዊት ገብሩ 'to David his servant' (ገብር 'servant', + -ሁ), alluding to Psalm 132:10 and 89:3. ወወሀቦ ዘይነብር ዲበ መንበረመለኮት: the printed መንበረመለኮት is one word, 'throne-of-divinity' (መንበር 'throne' + መለኮት 'divinity, godhead'); 'one who sits' (ዘይነብር) is Christ. እምዘርኡ በሥጋ እምድንግል 'from his seed in flesh, from a virgin' (the incarnation, Mary being of David's line). ወይኴንን ሕያዋነ ወሙታነ 'and he judges the living and the dead' (ኰነነ 'judge', imperfect ይኴንን; compare 2 Timothy 4:1, Acts 10:42). ወይፈድዮ ለኵሉ በከመ ምግባሩ 'and repays everyone according to his deed' (ፈድየ 'repay'; Romans 2:6, Psalm 62:12). ዘሎቱ ይደሉ ስብሐት 'to whom glory is fitting' (ይደሉ 'it is fitting'), a doxology ending with Amen; ለዓለመ ዓለም 'for ever and ever'. The unit is 29 words, a single long sentence.

sentences.t: ወበምድርኒ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ ዘይከውን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ዲበ ፡ ታቦተ ፡ ሕጉ ፡ ጽዮን ፡ ቅድስት ፡ ሰማያዊት ፡ ዘውእቱ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፤
sentences.l: And-on-earth-too he-gave-him one-who will-be king over ark-of his-law, Zion holy heavenly, who he king-of Ethiopia;
sentences.i: And on earth too he gave him one who would be king over the Ark of His law, holy, heavenly Zion, namely the king of Ethiopia;
sentences.n: ወበምድርኒ 'and on earth also' (ምድር 'earth', -ኒ 'also'), set against the heavenly kingship of the previous unit: Christ in heaven, the Ethiopian king on earth. ዘይከውን ንጉሠ ዲበ ታቦተ ሕጉ 'who will be king over the Ark of His law' (ዲበ 'upon, over'). ጽዮን ቅድስት ሰማያዊት 'Zion, holy, heavenly', in apposition: the Ark is Zion (the book's central idea; see ch. 33, unit 11). ዘውእቱ ንጉሠ ኢትዮጵያ 'who is the king of Ethiopia'. So the chain of the oath runs from David to Christ to the Ethiopian king.

sentences.t: ወእለሰ ፡ ይነግሡ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢኮኑ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ተዐድዎ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ወትእዛዝ ፡ ዘኢሠምረ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-those indeed who-reign, those who not-are Israel, transgressing law and-commandment which not-willed God. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: But those who reign, who are not Israel (?) — transgressing the law and the commandment, which God did not will. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.n: ወእለሰ ይነግሡ 'but those who reign' (እለ plural relative, -ሰ 'indeed, as for'). እለ ኢኮኑ እስራኤል 'who are not Israel, have not become Israel': I take it as a rebuke to the reigning line of Israel as unfaithful, perhaps in the light of Jeroboam's schism (1 Kings 12), but the phrase could also mean 'those not of Israel' (?). ተዐድዎ ሕግ ወትእዛዝ 'transgressing the law and the commandment' (ተዐድዎ the verbal noun of ተዐደወ with its object, as in ch. 9–12 and 13–16 and in the house entry; the alternative, a 3rd plural ተዐደዉ + -ኦ 'they transgressed it', is less likely (?)). ዘኢሠምረ እግዚኣብሔር 'which God did not will, was not pleased with'; whether this describes the law or the transgression is ambiguous (?). The four ፨ close chapter 34 and stay with the final unit.
